# Why Busy Bee saves outcomes in stage notes

**Finding:** retained evidence explains **durable worker-to-driver handoff and crash recovery**, and later explains the original-JSON envelope. It does **not** establish an original user decision choosing NOTES over DESCRIPTION, or a recorded comparison rejecting description/checkpoint-only storage. Notes was already the automatic-worker transport by the earliest direct contract review found here.

## Strongest chronology

1. **2026-10-10 — durable handoff rationale, initially advice.** **hv-37bs4, description, Action/outcome** recommends a “durable pre-close result for close/submit interruption.” Its Resolution separates native closure, accepted workflow result and request completion. This supports persistence before closure, not a documented reason for the particular field.

2. **2026-10-10 13:51:53Z — notes already an implementation contract.** **hv-x8oxn.1, comment 5374**, tan-lengthy-crayfish: “Current Busy Bee selects closed automatic tasks and immediately parses their notes as JSON”; otherwise “a collector can … see closed work without a usable result; a stopped worker may leave no result to recover.” The reviewed paper's close-before-publish order was rejected in favor of save-notes → close → finish, followed by driver collection. The reviewer explicitly calls this correction to an **existing** contract, not a new storage decision. It also identifies arbitrary manual-payload recovery as still unproved.

3. **2026-10-13 19:55:56Z — clearest explicit design rationale.** **hv-pr72s, comment 9275, §5 “Durable manual outcomes”**, moccasin-spiritual-earthworm, proposes: “Use the existing native task result location plus Busy Bee checkpoint history, not a Colony outbox.” Save `{choice,data}` before closure and “Put narrative verification in comments.” Reasons given:
   - retain original input so schema transforms are not applied twice;
   - avoid collision with a payload's own `choice` field and permit non-object schemas;
   - collect saved closed manual visits as well as automatic visits, so interruption/restart can recover the payload without replaying accepted progression.
   This was **architectural advice**, explicitly not adopted merely by filing. Alternatives actually mentioned: Colony outbox, two result protocols, and direct `next`/`choice`; **not** description versus notes. Comment **9289** (19:58:29Z) temporarily qualifies unified envelopes as optional because the parent's then-accepted scope retained automatic flat JSON. Do not erase that intermediate decision.

4. **2026-10-13 20:31:36Z — later unified split described as accepted and implemented.** **hv-gw9ag.4, comment 9404, finding 3** calls `{choice,data}` notes plus narrative comments “the new accepted contract.” It reports conflicting old narrative-notes instructions and `stage_result_conflict`, requiring correction rather than a legacy decoder. Its aligned findings explain that original-input envelopes preserve arbitrary-payload continuation. **hv-gw9ag.9, description** records completed corrective guidance/re-review. This demonstrates adoption as reported by reviewers/coordinator, **not a direct ct quotation selecting notes**.

5. **Later failures are consequences, not origin evidence.** **hv-ygcne.4.6.1.4, description** (October 14) records narrative notes colliding with result saving, then erroneous closure. **hv-sr1mr.2.2, description** (October 17) distinguishes an admitted ignored save-before-close instruction from an interface that exposed the ordering across commands. Summary response **hv-ii2hdt** reports the later ordered `complete` repair; **hv-0xei18** appropriately warns against treating these as unrepaired or population-level evidence.

## What this answers—and does not

Current contract corroborates the evolution: `/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/busybee/SPEC.md:13` reserves notes for original outcomes and comments for narrative; `:17` explicitly permits replacement-driver collection of arbitrary payloads. `:70` separately places engine snapshot/history in the checkpoint description.

**Inference:** stage notes provide a per-visit handoff artifact before the driver commits progression into checkpoint history; keeping narrative elsewhere makes that field machine-parseable. That explains the division of responsibilities. It does **not** prove notes was uniquely necessary: a dedicated description/result representation could conceivably have served the handoff. No retained explicit comparison or original human rationale for that field choice was found in this bounded evidence.

## Coverage

Selected local tracker only; examined records unchanged; no sync, maintenance or policy selection. Read all seven supplied lead descriptions, full primary comments 5374/9404 and hv-pr72s, selected relevant hv-37bs4 notes paragraphs, and full summary responses hv-0xei18/hv-ii2hdt. Exact-ID projected batch included closed/deferred, excluded `system`, returned nine records including ancestors, `has_more:false`. No closure-time cutoff; selected historical closures October 10–23, 2026. Literal `stage notes` discovery included closed/deferred and excluded `system`, oldest-first creation order, limit 30/offset 0, **has_more:true**; later pages were not inspected. No claim of exhaustive earliest origin, independent historical source/landing audit, or original user-transcript verification. An initial combined read timed out; its missing response was subsequently retrieved successfully. The remaining gap is the original field-selection decision, not the later durability rationale; pursuing it would require a separately focused older-history investigation.
response.title: Busy Bee stage-notes history: durability rationale, field-choice gap

# Checkpoint field history

**Bottom line:** There is retained original rationale for a **separate checkpoint bead**, but I found **no explicit comparison explaining lock-in-notes versus putting lock and snapshot together in one JSON description**. The earliest retained implementation plan already chooses notes for the lock. These are different evidentiary strengths.

## Strongest chronological evidence

1. **2026-10-04 — hv-8xl0.1, description** (closed 19:57 UTC): the early prototype called for “native br checkpoint persistence” and serialized-chart navigation. This establishes ancestry, not a field-choice rationale.

2. **2026-10-06, 19:25–19:35 UTC — hv-oe11, description/design/notes**, “POC 8: serialize workflow writes and expose input schemas.” This is the decisive original task record, authored by codex and recording an explicitly user-requested follow-up and authorized implementation delegation.
   - **Recorded problem / alternative actually displaced:** experiment 7 “stores the checkpoint in the visible workflow parent” and permits concurrent invocations to overwrite it; descriptions also mixed readable instructions, payload examples and metadata.
   - **Recorded authorized direction:** “Keep the workflow/epic and task briefs readable. Store machine checkpoint data on a separate automation-owned bead labelled system, attached by a native nonblocking related edge.” The description explicitly records user authorization for that system representation and runner access. This is an agent-authored record of user authorization, not a verbatim user transcript.
   - **Design:** “The system bead owns checkpoint and lock data; ordinary task descriptions retain instructions and a concise reference to CLI schema discovery.” Acquisition uses native conditional updates, a unique invocation token and fresh-state reads; task work occurs outside the short lock.
   - **Implementation choice, notes:** “Related system checkpoint holds persisted run; notes hold UUID lock acquired through if-unchanged CAS.” Completion notes confirm implementation and concurrent-process probes. **No stated reason here selects notes over one combined JSON description.** The task explains serialization, not that particular field split. It does not mention diagnostic PID placement.

3. **2026-10-06, 19:51–20:09 UTC — hv-0161, description/design**, consolidation into Busy Bee. It explicitly preserves the agreed “related system checkpoint, short native CAS lock” and promotes POC8 into the canonical library. This shows deliberate retention of the architecture, but supplies no new notes-versus-description argument.

## Current contract, not original rationale

`/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/busybee/SPEC.md:70` states snapshot and visit history live in description, lock UUID and diagnostic PID in notes. It explains separate readable work versus machine state, ordinary-selection exclusion by `system`, and nonblocking discovery through `related`. Line 74 documents conditional acquisition and ownership release. These explain current behavior; they do **not** establish that splitting JSON across two fields was necessary or explicitly compared with one description.

For settlement, `/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/busybee/SPEC.md:52` says a “run-note settlement intent fences further publication” and partial effects retain that intent. This is a documented purpose of the marker, not historical evidence explaining why the notes field was chosen. I did not locate original settlement field-selection rationale within this bounded pass.

## Classification and limits

- **Recorded user-authorized decision:** separate machine checkpoint from readable workflow/task briefs (hv-oe11).
- **Retained design:** checkpoint bead plus short conditional-update lock (hv-oe11 → hv-0161).
- **Implementation fact:** lock in notes, persisted run on checkpoint; present spec further identifies description and diagnostic PID.
- **Not established:** an original user decision or accepted alternatives analysis choosing notes over a single JSON description. I do not infer atomicity, convenience or independent writes as the reason.

Coverage: ordinary native searches included closed and deferred records and excluded `system`; no closure-time cutoff was imposed. Hydrated hv-8xl0.1, hv-oe11 and hv-0161 fully. Checkpoint/Busy-lock discovery pages were bounded (60 recent checkpoint, 35 earliest checkpoint, 25 earliest Busy-lock candidates); additional filtered pages of 15 settlement and 20 notes/lock candidates also reported more results. This is strongest-evidence research, **not exhaustive absence proof**. No reserved checkpoints, source-code history or original harness transcripts were inspected; no examined records were mutated or published remotely. If an exact original discussion is required, the next focused evidence would be the originating hv-oe11 conversation, not a storage redesign.
response.title: Checkpoint history: separate-bead rationale found; notes split unexplained

# Why Colony observations and Bee acknowledgments use comments

**Finding:** These are two distinct choices, not evidence of a general user decision that automation should prefer comments over descriptions/notes. Colony comments were a delegated implementation of Beads-only status; acknowledgment comments have an explicit accepted architectural rationale. I found no explicit description-versus-notes-versus-comments comparison.

## Strongest chronology and provenance

1. **Initial user direction: keep logs elsewhere.** `hv-3x8.9.1` description, historical “Decided by ct (hv-3x8.11 turns 7, 8, 10)” section: “colony writes clear logs to its own log, not spammed onto beads.” The same section leaves surfacing scheduling status “without spamming the bead” to design. `hv-3x8.17` (created 2026-10-04 06:03Z), description, CLI/status discussion: “Logs remain outside Beads”; the retained Q6 exchange accepts the **last recorded observation**, visibly distinguished from live state. The former is an agent-authored attribution to ct; the latter is the retained dialogue record. Neither explicitly selects comments.

2. **2026-10-04: prototype permits minimal summaries, delegates format.** `hv-e8i` description, “Mandate and isolation” delegates “ordinary implementation choices ... small schema decisions”; “Product contract” says: “Logs live outside Beads. Minimal last-observed request summaries may be written for Bee status, with timestamps/freshness.” Thus retaining small status facts was explicitly within the mandate, without revoking the separate-log rule.

3. **2026-10-04: actual observation-comment choice.** `hv-e8i.7.1` **design** records native CLI reconnaissance and the implementation contract: “latest native comment with Colony observation prefix is timestamped last evidence”; “Publish only changing minimal facts ... no logs or formula values; dedup by latest matching native comment, no new durable Beads metadata schema or status labels.” Its description requires Bee inspection through Beads only, without daemon/Colony SQLite. Closed 09:03:53Z, reason cites implementation `f597171` and native smoke verification. **Classification:** implemented, delegated choice—not a quoted human selection of comments. It explains the transport constraints and minimal-change approach, but does not explicitly reject description or notes.

4. **2026-10-04: stdout extends that existing model.** `hv-45f.9` description attributes narrowed stdout-only scope to ct and explicitly says “Reuse the existing Colony observation/publication model” with bounded cadence. Its **design** chooses “separate typed stdout activity comments ... for restart-safe throttling and offline request inspection.” Notes record changed-output publication capped at 30 seconds per attempt, initial/first output and settlement behavior, no silence heartbeat, and landing at `c023363348fb38a0d8d9266d2f63e592da79bfe9`. **Classification:** user-approved feature; comment format is the recorded implementation choice. This permits bounded metadata, not copying stdout/log bodies into Beads.

5. **2026-10-08: acknowledgment has a stronger explicit rationale.** `hv-45f.4` description retains the user's distinction between failure not resolved and failure “forgotten about”; `hv-45f.4.1` description quotes authorization to implement ack respecting actor/env. Neither user quote chooses the field. Consult `hv-45f.4.1.1` **notes**, “Recommendation” §1 and “Trade-offs and unresolved decisions,” states: “The native comment preserves append-only evidence and works offline”; labels lose actor/time/reason, rewriting close reason destroys failure classification, and recipe metadata/private SQLite put resolution in the wrong lifetime/authority. Native comment author/time supply attribution; JSON `{closedAt,reason}` binds acceptance to the exact failed closure. The proposed typed comment is explicitly identified there as a recommendation, not prior user direction. `hv-45f.4.1` **design** then says “Accepted librarian advice hv-45f.4.1.1” and adopts it. Closed 2026-10-08 18:41Z; notes record landing `ba872064a1968f39d3a56038805635ea35250a52`. **Classification:** accepted architectural advice, implemented—not merely a later explanation.

6. **2026-10-18: offline rationale later narrowed, storage not replaced.** `hv-yqmoa` description quotes ct: “there is no need for offline inspection ... no offline reads, we have a db. remove list for now”. Its accepted scope removes `bee list`, explicitly preserving exact-ID commands and making “No ... storage change”. Therefore the original offline-dashboard justification was deliberately retired; this record does **not** authorize removing observation or acknowledgment comments.

## Meaning, not merely location

Current contracts retain the separation: Colony observations are stale-able telemetry, not process or settlement authority. A matching `Bee acknowledgment:` comment is itself authoritative **resolution evidence**; it preserves failed outcome, task state and execution history. Projected labels support discovery. These comments cannot be treated as interchangeable logs.

**Inference, not recorded user rationale:** keeping the spawn description as its captured recipe and using separately attributed event records avoids mixing request intent with changing observations/acceptance. The acknowledgment consult supports that authority/lifetime distinction explicitly; no retained source here specifically analyzes mutable notes as an alternative.

## Coverage and limits

Read supplied design leads and focused ordinary historical records; all discovery excluded `system` and included closed/deferred work, with no closure-date cutoff. Initial bounded searches (25/30) reported additional matches; follow-up compact searches for acknowledgment/stdout/“Colony observation” used unlimited results, but only selected records were inspected. No reserved spawn records, production changes, policy adoption or tracker publication.

Original comment history on `hv-3x8.9.1`, `hv-3x8.17`, `hv-45f.4`, `hv-45f.4.1`, and `hv-45f.4.1.1` returned zero comments. Citations above are therefore **description/design/notes locations**, not invented comment IDs. Notes are mutable snapshots, not immutable original timestamps. `bee response get --task hv-45f.4.1.1` reported no filed response; its full retained consult is in notes. No historical response ID is available for that consult. Later cost reports `hv-iy8u3v`/`hv-shvp84` were not used to establish origins.

**Unresolved:** no explicit user choice of comments over description/notes, and no explicit decision superseding the keep-logs-elsewhere rule, was found. A broader source/transcript investigation would be a separate requested next step, not necessary to establish these retained precedents.

## Delivery/completion blocker

Research and authored delivery are complete; workflow completion is **blocked**, not done. `busybee complete hv-e25f78 hv-lfrphj next --json` succeeded, and native stage `hv-lfrphj` is closed (2026-10-24 10:26:54.995282Z). Its acceptance checklist is embedded in its description, not the native acceptance field; an attempted native checklist tick was refused without mutation. The report addresses all three embedded criteria.

The first `collect` exceeded its 90-second outer command budget. Retrying returned `checkpoint_locked` for `hv-q845lm`, owner `6b587278-9a07-48c4-ad54-129aea4d81cd`, PID `40533`, with no automatic expiry. Focused `ps -p 40533` returned no process; compact show still reports the run active and the closed stage as active. I did not steal the lock, close the run manually, or create a replacement run.

**Required next action:** the caller must explicitly authorize checkpoint recovery after inspecting the retained owner/partial effects, then resume **this same run** and collect its saved `next {}` outcome. Busy Bee must report `done` before successful execution completion. Until then the run remains open with a completed, durably delivered research result.
response.title: Historical findings complete; same-run collection blocked by retained checkpoint lock

response.author: red-vitreous-alpaca
response.body:
# Why responses became separate description-backed beads

**Bottom line:** ct explicitly preferred a dedicated response bead for focused retrieval and historical discovery. The immutable JSON envelope and precise comments/notes split were agent-designed implementation choices accepted in the feature—not retained verbatim user demands. I found no recorded consideration or rejection of putting everything in the producing task’s description.

## Strongest chronological evidence

1. **2026-10-14, 19:00:17Z — prior proposal, not policy.** Task **hv-tyagn**, peach-handsome-goldfish, local comment **10689**, ranked (1) producing-task comments, (2) description of a dedicated linked report bead, (3) ordinary-task notes. Comments won initially for per-entry author/time, append-oriented history, no extra record, and “no overwrite of assignment/design or Busy Bee result notes.” Dedicated descriptions were preferred when a report “must be fetched without task discussion,” providing durable identity and exact-ID projection, at the cost of extra records and correction/lifecycle rules. Notes were a growing mutable scalar lacking per-entry provenance; workflow notes were already reserved for machine outcomes. The report explicitly kept all options unapproved.

2. **2026-10-14 — user preference superseded that ranking.** **hv-s3faw.description** records the chosen dedicated filed response bead, nonblocking links, “clean minimal-noise retrieval from Bee and discoverable historical results.” **hv-qobsl.notes**, entry “final integrated architectural review hv-s3faw.9 / hv-s3faw.9.1,” preserves user excerpts: **“i like the sound of the dedicated bead”** and **“you might always want to handle historical records when searching”**. Attribution limit: the reviewing librarian says it read supplied verbatim user-intent excerpts; I read the retained archive, not the original conversation or excerpt file. This is stronger than the earlier explicitly paraphrase-only entries, but remains mediated evidence.

3. **2026-10-14 — agents specified the mechanics.** **hv-qobsl.description**, Resolution, attributes the concrete recommendation to librarian consultation **hv-s3faw.6.1**: immutable closed docs records, JSON description with body/provenance, atomic creation with nonblocking replies-to links, explicit corrections and ambiguity, exact execution lookup. The archive identifies black-gradual-spider’s delivery at **19:24:48Z, local comment 10798**, and source-attribution correction **10814** at 19:25:40Z. I did not separately rehydrate those two comments. Its stated difficulty: “task ownership, execution completion anchors, narrative delivery and workflow machine outcomes have different lifetimes; native comment IDs are not portable response identities.”

4. **Accepted implementation, not merely a recommendation.** **hv-s3faw.design** explicitly accepts immutable response JSON `{formatVersion,taskId,requestId?,author,body,supersedes}`, correction links, and no implicit latest-wins selection. It assigns complete answers to responses, concise progress/verification/pointers to comments, and original Busy Bee choice/data to stage notes. It also explicitly rejects automatic comments fallback, backfill and a response-required completion gate. **hv-s3faw**, codex, local comment **12379**, **2026-10-15 06:32:25Z**, records PR9 landing at `36026c5`; native closure follows at 06:34:41Z. Thus accepted implementation is evidenced, not fresh independent code verification.

## What the evidence does—and does not—explain

- **Separate response versus task description:** independent addressability, focused reads without discussion, discoverability and response provenance are explicit motivations. Preserving assignment/design rather than overwriting them is explicit in the initial comments-first proposal. Combining those points into a rationale against one mutable task-description container is **inference**: no examined source directly debates that exact alternative.
- **Immutable JSON inside response.description:** traceable to the librarian/coordinator contract and accepted feature design. It supplies portable identity, body/provenance and explicit correction semantics. The user preference for a dedicated bead does **not** establish that ct specifically requested JSON, immutability or each envelope field. No retained head-to-head justification for JSON versus plain Markdown in a dedicated description was found in this evidence window.
- **Narrative comments versus workflow notes:** this separation already existed before dedicated responses. hv-tyagn comment10689 identifies notes as protocol storage and cites an earlier concrete `stage_result_conflict`/premature-close recovery. hv-s3faw.design preserves that authority; comment **11436** (green-damaged-ostrich, **2026-10-14 20:10:05Z**) records five Land “notes -> comments wording fixes” without control-flow/schema changes. The response feature aligned guidance rather than originating structured workflow-result storage. This does not establish why notes, rather than another field, were originally selected for machine outcomes.
- **Later explanations are not origin evidence:** **hv-p779a**, **hv-bxfrn**, **hv-yanxl** (2026-10-15) address pruning, ownership and reachable help. **hv-3mhj** (2026-10-09) concerns librarian memory capture, not a general dedicated-response decision. **hv-0xei18** (2026-10-23) is retrospective process-friction synthesis, not original authorization.

## Coverage and limits

Read the supplied run/stage, ancestor descriptions, all six supplied historical leads, and two exact-ID follow-ups: hv-tyagn and hv-s3faw, including returned comments/design. Ordinary ancestor selection included closed/deferred records and excluded system; exact IDs required no pagination. No topic census, closure-time cutoff, raw-session recovery, source-code investigation or direct inspection of the cited consultation comments was performed. Selected origin records were created/closed October 14–15; later archive updates extend to October 24. Local comment numbers are conveniences: retain task, author, timestamp and quotation across clones.

**Unresolved for the workshop:** whether ct now wants the task description as a single container, and whether dedicated response JSON/immutability remains worthwhile. Historical adoption is not approval of current policy. No examined records, code, policy or remote tracker state were changed; only this research workflow/report is completed.
response.title: Dedicated responses: user preference versus agent-designed storage contract
